questions.knowledge_point: Checking Orthogonality of Sines and Cosines
questions.problem:
$$
⟨f(x),g(x)⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)g(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

Given the inner product on the set of continuous functions over $x\in [-\pi ,\pi )$ defined above, select the correct options below.$\,$
$⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)⟩=$
{{field-1}}

$\,$
The functions $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $g(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ 
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
We begin by using the half-angle identity

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡(3x)=\frac{1}{2}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)).
$$

Substituting this into the integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}x-\frac{1}{12}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)]}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\pi -(-\pi ))-\frac{1}{12}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\pi )-(\operatorname{sin}⁡(-6\pi )) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $g(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ $\text{are not orthogonal}$ with respect to the inner product.

questions.problem:
$$
⟨f(x),g(x)⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)g(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

Given the inner product on the set of continuous functions over $x\in [-\pi ,\pi )$ defined above, select the correct options below.

$\,$
$⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)⟩=$
{{field-1}}

$\,$
The functions $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)$ and $g(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)$ 
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
We begin by using the product-to-sum identity

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(9x)).
$$

Substituting this into the integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(9x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{18}\operatorname{sin}⁡(9x)]}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-3\pi ))+\frac{1}{18}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(9\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-9\pi )) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(0-0)+\frac{1}{18}(0-0) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)$ and $g(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)$ $\text{are orthogonal}$ with respect to the inner product.

questions.problem:
Let $F(x)={x}^{4}-7x$ for $x\in R,$ and let $f(x)$ be the $2\pi $-periodic extension of $F$ from $x\in [0,2\pi )$ to $x\in R.$ The Fourier series of $f$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)).
$$

Select the correct options in the expression for the coefficient ${a}_{3}$ below, where $⟨\,,⟩$ denotes the usual inner product on functions over $[0,2\pi ).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{3} & ={{field-1}} \\  & ={{field-2}}\,\cdot \,{{field-3}}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The usual inner product of functions $f$ and $g$ over $x\in [0,2\pi )$ is given by

$$
⟨f(x),g(x)⟩={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(x)g(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

For a $2\pi $-periodic function $f(x)$ that is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,2\pi ),$ the Fourier series of $f$ is given by 

$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)),
$$

where ${a}_{0},$ ${a}_{n},$ and ${b}_{n}$ are constants to be determined. 

Now, we find the inner product of $f(x)$ with $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩ & = \\ ⟨\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)),\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩ & = \\ ⟨\frac{{a}_{0}}{2},\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }⟨{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx),\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }⟨{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx),\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩ & = \\ \frac{{a}_{0}}{2}⟨1,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx),\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx),\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since the functions
$1,\operatorname{sin}⁡(x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x),…$
are orthogonal with respect to the defined inner product, the only nonzero term in the final expression above is

$$
{a}_{3}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩.
$$

Computing the inner product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{cos}^{2}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{1}{12}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\pi -0)-\frac{1}{12}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(12\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain that

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩ & ={a}_{3}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩ \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{⟨f(x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩}{⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)⟩} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2\pi }({x}^{4}-7x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $F(x)={x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}$ for $x\in R,$ and let $f(x)$ be the $2\pi $-periodic extension of $F$ from $x\in [-\pi ,\pi )$ to $x\in R.$ The Fourier series of $f$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)).
$$

Select the correct options in the expression for the coefficient ${b}_{1}$ below, where $⟨\,,⟩$ denotes the usual inner product on functions over $[-\pi ,\pi ).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & ={{field-1}} \\  & ={{field-2}}\,\cdot \,{{field-3}}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The usual inner product of functions $f$ and $g$ over $x\in [-\pi ,\pi )$ is given by

$$
⟨f(x),g(x)⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)g(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

For a $2\pi $-periodic function $f(x)$ that's piecewise continuous over $x\in [-\pi ,\pi ),$ the Fourier series of $f$ is given by 

$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)),
$$

where ${a}_{0},$ ${a}_{n},$ and ${b}_{n}$ are constants to be determined. 

Now, we find the inner product of $f(x)$ with $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩ & = \\ ⟨\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)),\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩ & = \\ ⟨\frac{{a}_{0}}{2},\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }⟨{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx),\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }⟨{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx),\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩ & = \\ \frac{{a}_{0}}{2}⟨1,\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx),\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx),\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since the functions
$1,\operatorname{sin}⁡(x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x),…$
are orthogonal with respect to the defined inner product, the only nonzero term in the final expression above is

$$
{b}_{1}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩.
$$

Computing the inner product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}x-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)]}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\pi -(-\pi ))-\frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )-(\operatorname{sin}⁡(-2\pi ))) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain that

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩ & ={b}_{1}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩ \\ {b}_{1} & =\frac{⟨f(x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩}{⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(x),\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)⟩} \\ {b}_{1} & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }\cdot {\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }({x}^{3}-3{x}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
⟨f(x),g(x)⟩={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(x)g(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

Given the inner product on the set of continuous functions over $x\in [0,2\pi )$ defined above, select the correct options below.$\,$
$⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)⟩=$
{{field-1}}

$\,$
The functions $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $g(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)$ 
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
We begin by using the product-to-sum identity

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(7x)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)).
$$

Substituting this into the integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(7x)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{14}\operatorname{cos}⁡(7x)+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =-\frac{1}{14}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(14\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))+\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{14}(1-1)+\frac{1}{2}(1-1) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $g(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)$ $\text{are orthogonal}$ with respect to the inner product.
